primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome with resistant hypertension and early ASCVD risk

medications.purpose: Control of hypertension (step 1 ACE‑I per NG136)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension in non‑Afro‑Caribbean adults <55
NICE NG136 recommends CCB as part of combination therapy for hypertension

medications.purpose: Add thiazide‑like diuretic to triple therapy for resistant hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 third‑line recommends indapamide MR as preferred thiazide‑like agent

medications.duration: Lifelong — monitor K+ & renal function 1‑2 weeks then 3‑monthly
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises adding spironolactone when BP uncontrolled on ACE‑I + CCB + diuretic

medications.purpose: Renal and cardiovascular protection in CKD/HF risk (NG106/TA902)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 & TA902 recommend SGLT2‑i for patients with CKD or HFrEF regardless of diabetes

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile 3 months after start then annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises statin therapy for patients with QRISK ≥10 % or metabolic‑syndrome‑driven risk

medications.medication: Metformin 500 mg once daily (titrate to 500 mg twice daily)
medications.dose: 500 mg PO daily, increase to 500 mg BID after 2 weeks if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — HbA1c review 3 monthly then annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for pre‑diabetes with high progression risk

medications.medication: Semaglutide 0.25 mg subcutaneous weekly (titrate to 1 mg weekly)
medications.dose: 0.25 mg SC weekly, increase to 1 mg weekly over 12 weeks as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — weight review 3 monthly then annually
medications.purpose: Weight management in severe obesity (BMI ≥ 40) per CG181
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 supports GLP‑1 RA for weight loss in severe obesity when lifestyle measures insufficient

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and rise in serum creatinine
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K+ and eGFR before start; repeat at 1‑2 weeks, then every 3 months

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentrations, raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Start atorvastatin 20 mg; monitor CK if muscle symptoms; consider lower statin dose if needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and thiazide‑like diuretic may reduce renal function
interactions_checked.action: Check renal function 1‑2 weeks after switch; continue monitoring annually

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential additive blood pressure lowering and volume depletion
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP and renal function; advise adequate hydration; hold dapagliflozin if eGFR falls <30

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in CKD and hypertension; can worsen renal function and raise BP (NG136)

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided; assumed ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m² for metformin and dapagliflozin dosing.
Serum potassium not provided; assumed ≤4.5 mmol/L before adding spironolactone.
Lipid profile not available; statin initiated based on high ASCVD risk inferred from metabolic syndrome.
HbA1c not provided; metformin initiation assumes HbA1c ≥48 mmol/mol or high‑risk prediabetes.
QRISK score not calculated; assumed ≥10 % given age, BMI, hypertension, smoking risk.
Allergy status unknown; assumed no contraindicating drug allergies.
treatment_summary: The plan intensifies antihypertensive therapy to a four‑drug regimen (ACE‑I, CCB, indapamide, spironolactone) per NICE NG136 for resistant hypertension, adds dapagliflozin for renal/cardiovascular protection (NG106), initiates atorvastatin for ASCVD risk reduction (CG181), starts metformin for high‑risk prediabetes (NG28), and introduces semaglutide for severe obesity (CG181). Monitoring of BP, renal function, electrolytes, lipids, HbA1c, and weight is outlined, with safety checks for hyperkalaemia and drug interactions.
